Middleware runs before every matched request, including static assets and redirects, so Next ships it on the lightweight edge runtime to keep it fast and close to the user. The cost is no full Node APIs (no fs, native modules, or most DB drivers), which is why it feels limiting. Newer Next versions let middleware opt into the Node runtime, but I'd check which version we're on before relying on that.
Action: check the Next version in apps/web/package.json and tell you whether the Node runtime option is available to us.

That's the classic cause: each line is probably rounded for display but the total sums unrounded values. Since unit prices are integer cents and quantity can be fractional (like 2.5 hours), I'll round each line to whole cents first and then sum the integers, so the total always matches the lines shown. Already-issued invoices keep their stored totals.
Action: find the totals computation in the api, round per line before summing, add a multi-line regression test with fractional quantities, and run the api tests.
